title: inventory-catalog-provenance-routing-matrix
content:
Purpose
-----
Working notes: define how node provenance and inventory catalog feed the routing policies in a multi-region control plane. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: list the label set we want, how health signals map to route weight/eligibility, and ownership of the inventory stream. Use for deduped discussion with serving-runtime and SRE.

Context / problem statement
-------------------------
- We need a single source-of-truth for "what capability lives where" (GPU type, memory, capacity, special accelerators) that the control plane and routing layer can query with low latency.
- The inventory is updated frequently (node joins, GPU failures, driver updates) and must balance freshness with scalability across regions.
- Routing decisions require both static capability info (labels) and dynamic health signals (GPU util, GPU temp, heartbeat staleness).
- Multi-region: we must avoid cross-region thrash and support explicit locality policies (data residency, latency SLOs).

Goals
-----
- Define label schema and provenance metadata (who set it, when)
- Provide a concise health-scoring algorithm that maps to routing eligibility + weights
- Describe inventory storage/streaming approach for control plane consumers (routing, autoscaler, console)
- Outline failure/fallback behavior for cross-region routing

Label schema (recommended canonical keys)
------------------------------------
- region: <string> (e.g., us-west1)
- az: <string> (e.g., us-west1-a)
- node_pool: <string> (e.g., model-small)
- hw.gpu_vendor: <string> (e.g., nvidia, amd)
- hw.gpu_model: <string> (e.g., a100-80gb, h100-80gb)
- hw.gpu_arch: <string> (e.g., ampere, hopper)
- hw.gpu_mem_gb: <integer-string> (e.g., "80")
- hw.gpu_count: <integer-string>
- hw.infer_accel: <string> (e.g., triton, onnxruntime-optim) optional
- capacity.reserved: <string> (e.g., "true"/"false")
- sku.tier: <string> (e.g., premium, base, spot-evictable)
- provenance.source: <string> (e.g., autoscaler, infra-provisioner, manual)
- provenance.version: <string> (inventory schema version)

Best practices / rules for labels
--------------------------------
- All hw.* keys are set by platform provisioning; mutable only by infra operators (provenance.source=infra-provisioner).
- capacity.reserved is set by Dedicated plane control when nodes are pinned to a customer.
- labels are immutable for capability attributes (gpu_model, gpu_mem) except in repair flows (reprovision).
- Every label write must include provenance metadata and a monotonic update id (for conflict resolution).

Inventory model & storage
-------------------------
Options considered:
1) Event-sourced log in a regional Kafka-like stream + periodic snapshots in a global, eventually-consistent store (Dynamo/Cockroach).
2) CRDT-based regional stores with gossip to reduce cross-region write latency.
3) Centralized control plane with strongly-consistent store (single leader) and read replicas per region.

Recommendation (pragmatic): hybrid approach
- Primary write path: regional event log (pub/sub) capturing node heartbeats, label changes, GPU telemetry samples.
- Periodic aggregator job (1min) consumes regional logs, produces a compact snapshot and health-score per node. Snapshots published to a globally-replicated metadata table (read-optimized) with TTL = 90s.
- For any control-plane action that must be strongly-consistent (customer pinning nodes), write-through to the central config store with synchronous replication to the regional caches.

Health signals (telemetry to capture)
------------------------------------
- heartbeat_ts (latest heartbeat ISO8601)
- gpu_util_pct (rolling 30s median)
- gpu_mem_used_gb (rolling 30s median)
- gpu_temp_c (rolling 30s max)
- gpu_ecc_errors (counter since boot)
- pci_error_count (counter)
- driver_ok (bool) [driver + CUDA version compatibility with runtime]
- nvlink_health (optional qualitative: good/warn/fail)
- process_hung_count (number of stuck infer processes)

Health scoring (simple weighted approach)
---------------------------------------
- Base health score = 100. Subtract weighted penalties:
  - heartbeat stale (>45s): -80 (ineligible)
  - gpu_util_pct > 95%: -40 (avoid for low-latency)
  - gpu_mem_free < 6%: -60
  - gpu_temp_c > 90C: -50
  - gpu_ecc_errors > 100: -70
  - driver_ok == false: -100 (ineligible)
- Node eligibility rule: health_score >= 40 -> eligible for most routes; >=75 -> preferred for latency-sensitive; <40 -> send to maintenance pool or warm-only routes.
- Note: thresholds tuned for A100/H100 baseline; create model-specific thresholds via config map.

Mapping health to routing behavior
---------------------------------
- eligibility boolean = health_score >= configured_min (default = 40)
- weight = clamp( (health_score / 100) * base_weight, min_weight ) where base_weight is derived from capacity and GPU count.
- For latency SLO routes, require health_score >= 75 and region latency RTT < configured_max.
- For cost-first routes (spot/evictable), accept health_score >=50 but block nodes with pci_error_count > 0 or high ECC error rate.

Routing policy matrix (summary)
-------------------------------
- Policy knobs: region_preference (list), capability_requirement (gpu_model/gpu_mem), cost_tier, privacy_constraints (must-stay-in-region), latency_SLO_ms, canary_percentage, fallback_strategy.
- Example row: {policy-id: low-latency-us-west, region_pref:[us-west1], capability:[h100-80gb], latency_SLO_ms:50, min_health:75, fallback:[same-region lower-capability, then us-east1/h100]}

Multi-region considerations and fallbacks
----------------------------------------
- Read locality: route maps and inventory snapshots should be read from nearest regional cache to avoid cross-region reads for every decision.
- Fallback precedence: local preferred -> other zone same region -> other region with warm pool -> remote cold pool.
- Cross-region cold start: before routing to a remote region for more capacity, check model variant compatibility (quantization allowed?) and warmup cost (estimated extra latency) and prefer warm nodes if warm_count > X.
- Avoid cascading failover: implement a circuit-breaker on region-level failover with backoff and cooldown windows (e.g., 30s initial cooldown, double on repeated fallovers).

Control plane responsibilities
-----------------------------
- Inventory ingestion (infra team): guarantee schema and provenance tags.
- Aggregator service (platform): compute per-node health score, build snapshots, expose read API.
- Router service (serving-runtime): consumes snapshots, applies policy matrix, selects node pool and weights.
- Autoscaler (platform): uses inventory topology + utilization to scale node pools; must avoid immediate decommissions if node passes health momentarily.
- Console & Alerts: surface nodes with low health_score, ECC trends, driver mismatches.

Consistency, versioning, and migrations
--------------------------------------
- Inventory schema has a version token (provenance.version). Router rejects snapshots with unknown schema versions.
- Rolling migration: if label keys change, accept both old and new keys for 2 weeks, then migrate policies.

Operational playbook (short)
---------------------------
- On heartbeat gap spike: check regional aggregator lag -> if lag > 60s, mark regional cache degraded, fall back to global table reads with rate-limit.
- On sudden wave of ECC errors: isolate nodes by setting health_score to -inf, create auto-ticket JIRA-PLAT-XXXX, notify infra on-call.
- Node repair flow: reprovision GPU driver -> wait for 5 successful heartbeats -> mark driver_ok true in snapshot.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- How do we surface label provenance in the Console UI without overwhelming non-technical users? (UX)
- Do we implement CRDTs for label merges or stick to event-log + last-write-wins with monotonic update ids? (consistency tradeoffs)
- Decide warm-pool sizing heuristics for cross-region fallbacks (SRE + serving-runtime follow-up).
- Perf: benchmark snapshot publish latency at 100k nodes across 6 regions. (perf ticket created: JIRA-PLAT-8423)

Action items
------------
- Evan: prototype regional aggregator that outputs per-node health score and snapshot (deadline: 2025-11-14).
- Aditi: write inventory schema v2 proposal doc (includes provenance.version changes) and link to Confluence (deadline: 2025-11-08).
- María: design Console mock for provenance viewing (deadline: 2025-11-20).

Notes to self
------------
- Keep label vocabulary small; prefer tags over free-text.
- Remember Dedicated needs stronger guarantees for reserved nodes: bump min_health and require synchronous write-through.
- Slack thread: #infra-inventory, pinged with initial draft 2025-11-02.

References
----------
- Confluence: SD & Inventory CR (see linked_artifacts)
- github PR: cluster-inventory prototype (see linked_artifacts)
- Jira: JIRA-PLAT-8423 (perf benchmark), JIRA-PLAT-8460 (canary fallback rules)

Revision history
----------------
- 2025-11-02: initial sketch (Aditi)
- 2025-11-05: added health-scoring draft, label provenance notes (Evan)
- 2025-11-10: added routing matrix and action items (Aditi + María)

End of doc
